messages:
anya: quick heads-up — started onboarding NeonVec v2 (contrastive-trained) for embeddings. ran the short-tail holdout and seeing recall@1 regress ~6% vs our current prod vectors. baseline (fp16) 0.845 -> neonv2-int8 0.782. not sure if it's quant or sampling differences.

ben: can you paste the exact eval command and the dataset split?

anya: sure, run we used:

```
eval run --model neonvec-v2 --quant int8 --dataset shorttail_holdout --metric recall@1 --normalize l2
```

output snippet:
```
Recall@1: 0.782
Recall@5: 0.914
mean_cos_sim_centroid: 0.62
```

ciara: did you try running the same with raw fp16 and with no L2? could be a normalization mismatch between index and query pipelines.

anya: fp16 run (same seed) returns Recall@1: 0.845. I ran with and without normalize: without L2 fp16 -> 0.841, without L2 int8 -> 0.779. suggests quant is the main hit but normalization also shifts numbers slightly.

samir: odd — clustering looked off in UMAP? any shift in centroids or intra-cluster variance?

anya: yes, quick UMAP visual shows class blobs more overlapped after int8. centroid cosine drop per class avg -0.05. purity down from 0.78 -> 0.71.

ben: could be scale/offset from per-channel quant. try per-channel vs per-tensor quantization and also run post-quant calibration with a larger sample.

anya: already tried perchannel int8 -> small gain: recall@1 0.794. still below baseline. calibration with 10k examples helps a bit.

ciara: what about the encoder's final norm/scale layer? sometimes folding or fused kernels change output scale under quant.

samir: let's run quick ablation: (1) perchannel int8 + calibration, (2) perchannel int8 + no final scale folding, (3) perchannel int4 (per-channel) w/ calibration. schedule: try (1) tonight, (2) @ben can you instrument the kernel folding check?, (3) @ciara can run int4 sweep tomorrow AM.

ben: yep will add logging for final linear scale and compare raw logits. I'll post diffs.

eval-bot: eval run complete for neonvec-v2 perchannel-int8-calib. recall@1: 0.801; recall@5: 0.920. artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/experiments/1798456000/neonvec-v2/p0001

anya: thanks! that's promising. still ~4.4% below fp16 baseline. will start a short anchor-sampling test to see if query distribution is skewing the metric. sharing configs in thread.

ciara: also recommend checking retrieval index building pipeline — check whether index vectors were written with different dtype or post-processing.

anya: noted. plan: run anchor-sampling experiment (10k anchors across shorttail/longtail) + rebuild index with perchannel-int8 vectors, compare recall breakdown by query length. will report results here by EOD.

samir: :thumbsup: keep it concise, and capture examples of failing queries for eval set.

anya: will do — posting preliminary table once done.
